html:
SMTO-GWT-0007 — SMTO couldn't confirm the computer got your stop or input request

GUID: 491f1a33-c903-468e-b4cd-f1b4e53f3358
Slug: gateway-control-error
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to stop work, or to type into a terminal on that computer, but no clear answer came back. The original work may still be running.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task: does it now show Stopped, or is it still working? For a terminal, check whether your input appears in its output. Your request may have arrived even though the answer got lost.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway's row. SMTO needs a working connection to see the work's real state and to send anything else.
  3. If the connection is back and the task is still running, select Stop once. For a terminal, send your input only if it isn't already there. Sending a stop or input only after checking avoids doubling up keystrokes or commands.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Stopped, or the terminal shows your input exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer. If the work still won't stop, ask them to check it directly on that computer; don't keep pressing Stop or resending input.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A cancellation or terminal control call (cancel, terminal write, session, input or detach) got an HTTP or connection error, or an unreadable reply, so the control outcome is unconfirmed and the operation may still be running.

What this means

  • A cancellation or terminal control call received an HTTP or transport error, or its reply could not be decoded as an object. This prevents confirmation of that control action. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A cancellation or terminal control call received an HTTP or transport error, or its reply could not be decoded as an object. This prevents confirmation of that control action.

How to diagnose it

  • Match the failed control call to the original operation and distinguish a rejection from a lost or malformed acknowledgment.

How to fix it

  • Restore the Gateway connection, then read the operation's current status (job or terminal session state) on the Gateway before sending another cancel or terminal request. The failed call is identified in Technical details; never assume the control action did or did not take effect.
  • Reconnect the gateway and inspect the operation's current status before sending another control request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation's status or terminal session confirms the requested control outcome before another control attempt.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
  • SMTO-GWT-0013 — Gateway identity changed
  • SMTO-GWT-0005 — Gateway unauthorized
  • SMTO-GWT-0006 — SMTO got a message from the Gateway it couldn't trust
